rules.sentence: A study of 91 patients identified that close to 60% of these patients had anatomical changes in the cubital tunnel that caused the ulnar nerve neuropathy, of which nearly 20% of patients had a subluxation of the ulnar nerve.
Other causes identified in this study were osteophytes in almost 7% of patients and luxation of the ulnar nerve in nearly 10% of patients.
Post-traumatic lesions also can cause symptoms in about 3.3% of patients.[2]
Ulnar nerve neuropathy is the second most common compression neuropathy of the arm, following carpal tunnel syndrome.
The exact pathophysiology of cubital tunnel syndrome is unknown.
